newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The five government parties, despite fresh rifts caused by the censure debate, have agreed to remain allied in order to block the Democrats' resurgence and form a post-election coalition. (THE NATION)

- Three out of four fish examined at Unocal's Erawan platform have unnaturally high concentrations of mercury and nearly 12 percent have mercury levels above the standard fit for human consumption. Unocal officials, however, say it will be premature to reach any conclusions based on the data because there are some questions about the way it was gathered and analysed. (THE NATION)

- A high pressure front from China will bring heavy rain to Bangkok in the next couple of days. Bangkok Governor Bhichit Rattakul has expressed concern that the front might have a severe impact on Bangkok if it coincides with another low-pressure front in the North. (BANGKOK POST)

- Top executives of Siam Commercial Bank, Thai Farmers Bank and Bangkok Bank have vowed their third quarter earnings will be better than expected in an unprecedented move to preempt another market nosedive that could result from expected negative financial reports. (THE NATION)

- The Commerce Ministry agrees a Board of Investment surcharge imposed on foreign steel dumping has had a negative impact. The ministry has told the cabinet that although the surcharge can be immediately applied, application is restricted to products not tied to World Trade Organisation regulations. (BANGKOK POST)
